title: Spectral Guidance for Flexible and Efficient Control of Diffusion Models
claim: One fixed learned feature basis can steer sampling toward any chosen subset of conditioning classes without retraining.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, shared legend on top, density contours as background
description: A shared legend runs across the top: six colored dots for classes y=0 to y=5 and a white-filled dot for generated samples. Below are three square panels with the same blue-green contour map of a 2-D Gaussian mixture log-density. Panel (a), labeled Prior, shows six clusters of colored points, one per class, spread over the density modes. Panel (b), labeled y ∈ {4,2,1}, shows only white generated points concentrated in the three matching modes. Panel (c), labeled y ∈ {3,5}, shows white points only in the two corresponding modes. The eye goes first to the colorful prior cluster, then to the white clusters that move with the label subset. The captions use math notation for the conditioning sets.
caption: Spectral Guidance on a Gaussian mixture prior. Contours depict $\log p_0(x_0)$. (a) Prior samples colored by component. (b, c) Samples generated by spectral guidance (white) conditioned on different label subsets, using a fixed set of $K=30$ spectral modes. The same features enable sampling from $p(x_0\mid y\in\mathcal{Y})$ for arbitrary conditioning sets $\mathcal{Y}$.
abstract: We introduce Spectral Guidance, a framework for controlling diffusion models by leveraging the intrinsic geometry of the generative process. As data is progressively corrupted by noise, only a small number of features remain informative for control. We characterize them as the singular functions of a conditional expectation operator and show that they can be learned via a self-supervised objective. Once recovered, this basis enables the projection of arbitrary guidance signals, such as labels, CLIP embeddings, or masks, directly onto the sampling trajectory. This approach allows for stable, high-fidelity control without retraining or denoiser backpropagation during sampling. Empirically, we improve conditional accuracy on CIFAR-10 by 37 percentage points over the strongest training-free baseline while offering $4\times$ faster sampling. Moreover, the same representations that support label and CLIP guidance also enable spatial control, such as mask-based guidance, without auxiliary models. Finally, our framework reveals a phase transition in the generative process, pinpointing the optimal time window for effective guidance.
